source_caption:
𝐀𝐒 𝐅𝐀𝐑 𝐁𝐀𝐂𝐊 𝐀𝐒 𝐈 𝐂𝐀𝐍 𝐑𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐌𝐁𝐄𝐑 ⁣
⁣
Some movies you watch once and move on. Even good ones. But 𝐆𝐨𝐨𝐝𝐟𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐬 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟎)? I’ve been watching that movie my whole damn life. I first saw it when I was ten years old and the opening line burned into my brain forever: “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster.” And honestly, from that moment on, I was hooked. Hooked in a way that fifteen rewatchings later, I still get the same chills. ⁣
⁣
Marty doesn’t make mobsters look like godlike dons in smoky offices (that’s The Godfather’s territory). He’d only made the movie because he read Nicholas Pileggi’s “Wiseguy”, and literally called him to say, “I’ve been waiting for this book my entire life.” Pileggi’s response? “I’ve been waiting for this phone call my entire life.” That’s destiny, right there.⁣
⁣
It’s been 36 years and 𝐆𝐨𝐨𝐝𝐟𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐬 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟎) hasn’t aged a second. If anything, it’s only grown sharper, funnier and more iconic. Every gangster movie made since lives in its shadow and most look cartoonish by comparison. Watching it again feels like coming home to chaos. Like slipping into a world you know is poison but can’t resist. Goodfellas (1990) is the ULTIMATE mob movie. The one that makes you remind you: never rat on your friends, and always keep your mouth shut.

source_details.synopsis: Goodfellas (stylized as GoodFellas) is a 1990 American biographical gangster film directed by Martin Scorsese, written by Nicholas Pileggi and Scorsese, and produced by Irwin Winkler. It is a film adaptation of Pileggi's 1985 nonfiction book Wiseguy. Starring Robert De Niro, Ray Liotta, Joe Pesci, Lorraine Bracco and Paul Sorvino, the film narrates the rise and fall of Mafia associate Henry Hill and his friends and family from 1955 to 1980. Scorsese initially titled the film Wise Guy and postponed making it; he and Pileggi later changed the title to Goodfellas.
